source.title: Slot-Loaded Microstrip Patch Sensor Antenna for High-Sensitivity Permittivity Characterization

evidence: PDF page 3: Figure 1 topology and statement that the antennas were designed for 2.5 GHz under unloaded conditions.
PDF page 4: conventional geometry/material values and Figure 2 S11 plot.
PDF page 5: scaled slot-loaded geometry values, resonances, -10 dB bandwidths, fractional bandwidths, and quality factors.
Geometry and nominal resonance: explicit prose on PDF page 4.
Bandwidth, fractional bandwidth, and quality factor: explicit prose on PDF page 5.
Geometry, resonances, first bandwidth, fractional bandwidth, and quality factor: explicit prose on PDF page 5.
The feed width equality wf3 = wf1 links the 1.66 mm value on PDF pages 4-5.

unscaled_slot_loaded_patch.note: Included only to disambiguate the blue Figure 2 trace; it is not one of the two primary validation cases in this target file.

use_restrictions: Use the digitized red trace only for qualitative shape checks or a deliberately loose visual comparison.
Do not replace the text-derived first-resonance frequency and bandwidth targets with raster-derived values.
Do not use the conventional visible-only CSV for resonance, minimum-S11, bandwidth, or full-curve RMSE validation.
The red first-resonance minimum reaches the -30 dB plot floor, so the actual minimum is unresolved at or below -30 dB.

unresolved_from_paper: Port type and exact port geometry.
Open/radiation boundary type and air-box clearance.
Frequency sweep type, step size, and interpolation settings.
Exact conductor loss model and surface roughness.
The second-resonance -10 dB bandwidth of the scaled slot-loaded antenna.

recommended_validation_policy.geometry: Require the published nominal values and Figure 1 topology; record any coordinate convention as an implementation assumption.
recommended_validation_policy.electromagnetic_primary: Use the explicit text-derived resonance frequencies and -10 dB band edges as primary targets.
recommended_validation_policy.electromagnetic_secondary: Use Figure 2 digitization only as a visual/shape diagnostic because line width, clipping, and curve overlap dominate narrow-band error.
recommended_validation_policy.cross_solver_note: HFSS-to-CST differences must not be attributed to geometry until the unresolved port, boundary, conductor, mesh, and sweep assumptions are documented.
